title: Secrets of Scotland Yard
identity_notes: British true-crime anthology built from dramatizations of actual crimes and Scotland Yard investigations. Contemporary evidence documents a 52-part international run by May 1948, while later surviving copies carry Towers of London syndication numbers/dates and a separate 60-entry 1957 package order. These distribution layers are preserved separately rather than forced into one canonical chronology.

eras.notes: New Zealand Listener announces 52 half-hour programs starting May 7, 1948.

eras.label: Later Mutual U.S. rebroadcast/package era

historical_context.title: Postwar public appetite for true crime
historical_context.description: The series dramatized real criminal cases during a postwar period of strong popular interest in true-crime reporting and police investigation.

historical_context.title: International transcription syndication
historical_context.description: A British independent production circulated internationally by transcription rather than belonging to one original national network schedule.

historical_context.title: Scotland Yard and forensic authority in popular culture
historical_context.description: Episodes repeatedly foreground Scotland Yard detectives, forensic clues, identification, pathology and courtroom evidence.

historical_context.title: Later American rebroadcast life
historical_context.description: Selected recordings were repackaged for later U.S. Mutual circulation, demonstrating the long afterlife of transcribed radio drama.
